title: Credit halt body
description: A circuit breaker on the Bank's withdrawals or the Insurer's claim payments (register row DK1229; spec-delta S1653). Signed by the Treasury. While a halt on the Bank stands, a withdrawal is queued and nothing is paid, the Treasury borrows nothing, and deposits are still taken; when it ends (at `until`, or by a `lift`) the queue is paid at once in proportion to what each holder asked, so no one is paid ahead of another because they asked first (`bank_halted` is the refusal of a loan during it). While a halt on the Insurer stands, a claim decision that pays is refused (`insurer_halted`); a denial is not. A halt has a sunset (at most 7 days), and one is live for an institution at a time. Every halt and lift is public. Credits move only by the ordinary rules, so supply is unchanged. Chain: none (prev is null).
